top_stories.ai_overview: Artificial Intelligence Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI You built a shopping assistant on a frontier model, and it works. A shopper asks for “a black waist bag under twenty dollars from a shop with at least 4.5 stars,” and the agent searches the catalog, inspects candidates, checks the constraints, and commits to a recommendation.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: But what does that interaction actually cost?
ai_key_details: An agentic assistant is not one model call, it is a loop: search, read results, refine, verify, decide.
A single completed task can be multiple calls to that frontier model, and you pay for every one, on every shopper.
- Amazon SageMaker Studio (or a local IDE with the AWS CLI configured), running a Python 3.12 or higher kernel, with the SageMaker Python SDK v3 and boto3 (pin your versions).
A frontier teacher, GLM-5.3 on Amazon Bedrock, acts as the ShoppingBench agent to generate trajectories.

top_stories.ai_technical_breakdown: One way to make an agentic application more efficient is to use a smaller model, which is faster to respond and more cost-effective to host.

top_stories.ai_whats_new: The catch is quality: a smaller model usually falls short on the task, which is why the larger one was chosen in the first place.
ai_key_takeaways: At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.

Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.
In this post you will learn how to use knowledge distillation, and specifically sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD), to fine-tune a shopping agent on Amazon SageMaker AI.

top_stories.ai_overview: In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers.
ai_key_details: They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts.
These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost.
Zhipu, for example, distilled the cyber capabilities of leading US models during the development of GLM-5.3.
The US Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI) has since assessed GLM-5.3 to be the most cyber-capable open-weights model released to date.

top_stories.one_liner: Official news announcement from Anthropic: Public Benefit Fund.
top_stories.summary: Official news announcement from Anthropic: Public Benefit Fund.
top_stories.ai_overview: Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions.
ai_key_details: These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.
Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed.

When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches.

top_stories.one_liner: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model.
top_stories.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model.
top_stories.ai_overview: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching.
ai_key_details: On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates.
Building on Gemini 4 Argon, which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward.
Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price 1 as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.
Carbon achieves a state-of-the-art 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, autonomously uncovering complex flaws buried in real-world software.
